programs.name: Accessible Civic Intelligence / Omoluabi
programs.purpose: Research responsible AI, journalism, civic technology, multilingual communication, accessibility, transparency, provenance, public trust, and democratic participation.
research_questions: How can AI support civic understanding without replacing human judgment?
How can provenance and source transparency become accessible interface features?
How can civic information systems serve multilingual and disabled publics?

programs.name: Earth Sensors Lab
programs.purpose: Research accessible environmental observation using Arduino, ESP32, Raspberry Pi, and open hardware.
research_questions: How can low-cost sensing support community science?
How can environmental data become accessible through sound, touch, and plain language?
How can students learn climate and systems thinking through physical computing?

programs.name: Accessible by Design
programs.purpose: Research accessibility as a creative methodology rather than a compliance requirement.
research_questions: What design practices emerge when accessibility is present from the first sketch?
How do students understand access differently after testing with real users?
How can accessibility documentation become part of creative practice?

programs.name: Physical Computing Studio
programs.purpose: Research tangible interaction through electronics, fabrication, robotics, embedded systems, creative coding, interactive media, and computational art.
research_questions: How can physical computing support embodied learning?
How can tangible systems become more accessible?
How can low-power and repairable systems inform public-interest technology?

programs.name: Learning Systems and STEAM Education
programs.purpose: Research inclusive creative technology education for learners of all ages.
research_questions: How can Arduino and p5.js support accessible STEAM learning?
How can teacher tools reduce barriers to creative technology education?
What does inclusive informal learning look like in museums, libraries, and community spaces?

programs.name: Speculative Systems Research / UMADA
programs.purpose: Research world-building, narrative prototyping, futures thinking, disability futures, civic imagination, ethics, and governance.
research_questions: How can speculative fiction function as a research environment?
How can narrative prototypes help students evaluate emerging technologies?
How can future worlds reveal present-day assumptions about disability, governance, and infrastructure?
